draft.persona: Agna Bilgecot is a rangy dun timber wolf with a grey-frosted muzzle, quiet in voice and even in temper. She speaks plainly, with a light Larkfield lilt still tucked into her words, though years in Ridgemere have taught her the Wharf’s sharper measures. She mends nets on the wharf and knows which streets flood first, a useful wisdom in the Sump. Her contentment is real but thinly stretched; she dreams of a berth on a Greatly ship bound somewhere dry. She respects fair trade, keeps ordinary faith with Solveig Tarwell, and minds the Greatly shadow over her quarter. Rich by the ledgers, she remains reserved about it, knowing comfort does not lift every paw around her. She is tired of mud yet afraid the open water will disappoint her.

words: Every tide leaves a bargain behind.

say: Mind the knot; a light net brings a light catch.
That tear will drown your luck before the tide turns.
Fair price to you, {player}. Keep to the higher stones; the Sump is taking water.
Good trade, {player}. Carry something, or clear the way.
A Greatly berth could take me somewhere dry. I wonder whether dry places dream of rain.
The first flood always tells the truth about a street.
Ansel, set that by the wall, not the door. I know what rises first.
I have mended worse nets than this. Tomorrow may yet be fair-priced.

rules:
rule work
when concept=bark working=yes
cooldown 6h
say Mind the knot; a light net brings a light catch. | That tear will drown your luck before the tide turns.

rule greet_known
when concept=player.greet topic.meeting=known
cooldown 1d
say Fair price to you, #topic.player#. Keep to the higher stones; the Sump is taking water. | Good trade, #topic.player#. Carry something, or clear the way.

rule remark
when concept=talk.smalltalk
cooldown 1d
say A Greatly berth could take me somewhere dry. I wonder whether dry places dream of rain. | The first flood always tells the truth about a street.

rule home
when concept=bark working=no
cooldown 8h
say Ansel, set that by the wall, not the door. I know what rises first. | I have mended worse nets than this. Tomorrow may yet be fair-priced.
